territorial_scope.description: Applies with general observance throughout Mexico, requires security agencies of the states and Mexico City to cooperate, and allows interconnection with foreign governments and companies under agreements.

summary.short: Establishes Mexico's Sistema Nacional de Investigación e Inteligencia en Materia de Seguridad Pública: a CNI-operated Plataforma Central de Inteligencia interconnecting public security databases and, under conditions, other records, with AI tools permitted in analysis. Binding nationwide; in force the day after DOF publication, 16 July 2025.
summary.long: The Law creates the Sistema Nacional de Investigación e Inteligencia en Materia de Seguridad Pública, coordinated by the Secretaría de Seguridad y Protección Ciudadana and operated by the Centro Nacional de Inteligencia (CNI). The Consejo Nacional, chaired by the federal Executive, may issue agreements of mandatory observance for all Mexican authorities. The CNI runs the Plataforma Central de Inteligencia, to be connected in real time to listed public security systems and, on request or by agreement, to other public bodies, certain private persons and foreign entities. Private holders of relevant databases must collaborate in their transmission, consultation and supply; private entities may only grant the CNI access to specified systems under an agreement. Intelligence processing may use automation and artificial intelligence tools. Information must be encrypted and access controlled by user levels; personnel must be certified and subject to trust controls. Unauthorized disclosure of confidential information is punishable under administrative and criminal legislation. Data handling must follow federal transparency and personal data laws. The Platform must begin full operation within 180 working days of entry into force.

notes: Decree adopted 1 July 2025 and published 16 July 2025; in force the day after publication (Transitorio Primero). Possible internal inconsistencies: Art. 9 III and Art. 14 use 'Consejo Nacional de Seguridad Pública', while Art. 2 II defines 'Consejo Nacional de Inteligencia en Seguridad Pública' and elsewhere the text uses 'Consejo Nacional'; Art. 11 uses both 'Gabinete Federal de Seguridad Pública' and 'Gabinete Federal de Seguridad'; 'Consejo de Seguridad Nacional' (Arts. 3, 9, 19) is not defined in this text. Target instrument IDs are null because the relations are to laws not identified in the registry metadata. No other law is amended or repealed by this text.

thresholds.note: The text contains no numeric cutoff that changes legal treatment of a person, entity or service. The only numbers are procedural time limits (Transitorios Tercero, Cuarto, Quinto, Sexto: 180 and 90 días hábiles, 180 días; art. 14 and 45: reports every six months), which the codebook classifies as deadlines (events), not thresholds. No monetary, size, user-count or compute cutoffs were found.
